title: 中学
description: 适合 12-16 岁，有一定英语基础的孩子。全部取自 TED-Ed 的动画短片，每集 5-7 分钟，选题横跨科学、历史、生活技能与语言现象。相比小学的童话，这里开始出现从句和复合结构，词汇也进入抽象层面（psychological、perceive、adaptation）。配音接近正常语速，是孩子从「学英语」走向「用英语学东西」的过渡材料。
descriptionEn: For children aged 12-16 with some English foundation. All episodes are TED-Ed animated shorts, 5-7 minutes each, spanning science, history, life skills and language itself. Compared with the younger set's fairy tales, these bring subordinate clauses and complex structures, and vocabulary moves into the abstract (psychological, perceive, adaptation). Narration is close to normal speed — a bridge from 'learning English' to 'learning things in English'.

items.episode: The fascinating reason you loved peek-a-boo
items.englishName: The fascinating reason you loved peek-a-boo
items.description: 最短最轻松的一集。开头罗列各国对躲猫猫的叫法，再讲它为什么能让婴儿发笑。出现 hold up、take turns 等短语动词，适合作为中学第一批的入门。
items.descriptionEn: The shortest and lightest episode. Opens with the game's names across languages, then explains why it delights infants. Phrasal verbs like hold up and take turns — a gentle start to this set.

items.episode: Why does catnip make cats go crazy?
items.englishName: Why does catnip make cats go crazy? - Jaap de Roode
items.chineseName: 猫薄荷为什么让猫发疯
items.description: 讲猫薄荷里的化合物如何影响猫的大脑。生物与化学词汇集中（compound、receptor、evolution），因果关系说得很清楚，是练习「因为所以」表达的好材料。
items.descriptionEn: How a compound in catnip acts on a cat's brain. Dense with biology and chemistry terms (compound, receptor, evolution) and very clear cause-and-effect phrasing.

items.episode: How a broken heart affects your body
items.englishName: How a broken heart affects your body
items.chineseName: 心碎如何影响你的身体
items.description: 从情绪说到真实的生理反应。医学词汇较多（syndrome、hormone、vessel），比喻说法与客观描述交替出现，能学到同一件事的两种讲法。
items.descriptionEn: From emotion to genuine physical response. Plenty of medical vocabulary (syndrome, hormone, vessel), alternating figurative language with clinical description.

items.episode: What toys have kids played with throughout history?
items.englishName: What toys have kids played with throughout history?
items.description: 几千年来孩子玩什么。时间顺序的表达很密集（for millennia、by the 19th century），是练习梳理时间线的一集。
items.descriptionEn: What children have played with over thousands of years. Heavy on sequencing and time expressions (for millennia, by the 19th century) — good practice for following a timeline.

items.episode: Should you rinse your dishes before placing them in the dishwasher?
items.englishName: Should you rinse your dishes before placing them in the dishwasher? - Rachel Yang
items.chineseName: 洗碗前到底该不该冲水
items.description: 从一个生活小问题讲起，正反两面论证。口语化程度高，含有 whether or not、it depends 这类讨论句型。
items.descriptionEn: A small everyday question argued from both sides. Very colloquial, with discussion patterns like whether or not and it depends.

items.episode: 4 ways to fix your attention span
items.englishName: 4 ways to fix your attention span - Shannon Odell
items.chineseName: 修复注意力的 4 个方法
items.description: 讲注意力是怎么被切碎的，以及四个可行的办法。跟孩子自己的学习直接相关，祈使句和建议句型（try doing、instead of）反复出现。
items.descriptionEn: How attention gets fragmented, and four workable fixes. Directly relevant to a student's own study habits, with repeated imperatives and advice patterns (try doing, instead of).

items.episode: 4 ways to tell a great story
items.englishName: 4 ways to tell a great story
items.chineseName: 讲好一个故事的 4 个方法
items.description: 拆解故事为什么打动人。叙事类词汇（narrative、tension、pacing），说明文结构清晰，对写作也有帮助。
items.descriptionEn: A breakdown of why stories move us. Narrative vocabulary (narrative, tension, pacing) with a clear expository structure that also helps with writing.

items.episode: Do we actually know how magnets work?
items.englishName: Do we actually know how magnets work? - Rachel Yang
items.chineseName: 我们真的知道磁铁怎么工作吗
items.description: 层层设问推进，最后落到量子层面。物理术语有难度（electromagnetic、quantum、field），但每问一句就答一句，跟着问题走不容易掉队。
items.descriptionEn: Advances through a chain of questions down to quantum mechanics. The physics terms are demanding (electromagnetic, quantum, field), but each question is answered in turn.

items.episode: Meet the slow loris, the only venomous primate in existence
items.englishName: Meet the slow loris, the only venomous primate in existence - Stephanie A. Poindexter
items.chineseName: 认识懒猴：唯一有毒的灵长类
items.description: 介绍一种很少人知道的动物。描述性形容词丰富（venomous、nocturnal、deliberate），是扩充形容词储备的好材料。
items.descriptionEn: Introduces a little-known animal. Rich in descriptive adjectives (venomous, nocturnal, deliberate) — good for building descriptive vocabulary.

items.episode: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales
items.englishName: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales - Claudia Schwabe
items.chineseName: 迪士尼童话的黑暗起源
items.description: 对照格林兄弟原作与迪士尼改编。改编类词汇（adaptation、sanitize、grim），大量「原作如何、电影如何」的对比句式。跟小学那批童话正好呼应。
items.descriptionEn: Compares the Grimm originals with Disney's adaptations. Adaptation vocabulary (adaptation, sanitize, grim) and constant 'in the original / in the film' contrasts — a nice echo of the younger fairy-tale set.

items.episode: The missing ingredient in how we learn
items.englishName: The missing ingredient in how we learn
items.description: 讲学习中那个常被忽略的东西是什么。认知科学词汇（metacognition、struggle、retrieval），转折多（actually、instead），整篇是论证而不是讲故事。
items.descriptionEn: On the overlooked element in learning. Cognitive-science vocabulary (metacognition, struggle, retrieval) with frequent turns (actually, instead) — this is argument rather than storytelling.

items.episode: 5 sneaky ways stores get you to spend more
items.englishName: 5 sneaky ways stores get you to spend more
items.chineseName: 商店让你多花钱的 5 个套路
items.description: 消费心理的五种常见手法。通篇用 you 直接对读者说话，商业与心理词汇（perceive、comparison、psychological）结合得自然，实用性很强。
items.descriptionEn: Five common tactics of consumer psychology. Addresses the reader as 'you' throughout, weaving commercial and psychological vocabulary (perceive, comparison, psychological) naturally.

items.episode: The Greek myth of Apollo's curse
items.englishName: The Greek myth of Apollo's curse - Iseult Gillespie
items.chineseName: 希腊神话：阿波罗的诅咒
items.description: 希腊神话故事。专有名词密集（Oracle、Delphi、nymph），过去时叙述为主，措辞比其他集更文学化一些。
items.descriptionEn: A Greek myth. Dense with proper nouns (Oracle, Delphi, nymph), mostly past-tense narration, and somewhat more literary in style than the rest of the set.

items.episode: How to attack (and defend) a medieval castle
items.englishName: How to attack (and defend) a medieval castle - Connor C. Wilson
items.chineseName: 如何攻下一座中世纪城堡
items.description: 攻城与守城的博弈。军事历史词汇多（trebuchet、moat、siege），攻守双方交替陈述，对立句式很清晰。
items.descriptionEn: The back-and-forth of siege and defence. Heavy military-history vocabulary (trebuchet, moat, siege), with attackers and defenders stated in turn.

items.episode: What is sumo, and why is it so popular?
items.englishName: What is sumo, and why is it so popular? - Lee Thompson
items.chineseName: 相扑是什么，为什么这么受欢迎
items.description: 介绍日本相扑的规则与文化。外来文化专有词（yokozuna、dohyō、ritual），包含大量「解释陌生概念」的常用表达。
items.descriptionEn: Introduces the rules and culture of Japanese sumo. Loanword proper nouns (yokozuna, dohyō, ritual) plus plenty of stock phrases for explaining unfamiliar concepts.

items.episode: When did we start using passports?
items.englishName: When did we start using passports? - Kristin Surak
items.chineseName: 护照是什么时候开始用的
items.description: 护照这种证件是怎么一步步变成今天这样的。制度类抽象名词多（document、border、identity），适合接触社会议题类英语。
items.descriptionEn: How the passport became what it is today. Plenty of abstract institutional nouns (document, border, identity) — an introduction to English about social systems.

items.episode: Red gold: The world's most expensive spice
items.englishName: Red gold: The world's most expensive spice - Carolyn Beans
items.chineseName: 红色黄金：世界上最贵的香料
items.description: 藏红花的种植、贸易与造假。农业经济词汇（harvest、thread、counterfeit），数字、重量、价格的表达密集。本批最长的一集。
items.descriptionEn: The cultivation, trade and counterfeiting of saffron. Agricultural-economy vocabulary (harvest, thread, counterfeit) with dense numbers, weights and prices. The longest episode in this set.

items.episode: Why do we use "they" as a singular pronoun?
items.englishName: Why do we use "they" as a singular pronoun? - Arika Okrent
items.chineseName: 为什么把 they 当作单数代词
items.description: 讲英语语法本身的演变。语言学词汇（pronoun、gender-neutral、syntax），引用大量历史例句。是本批唯一直接谈英语语言现象的一集，放在最后收尾。
items.descriptionEn: On how English grammar itself evolves. Linguistic vocabulary (pronoun, gender-neutral, syntax) with many historical examples quoted. The only episode in this set about English itself — a fitting close.
